Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is Gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP is an effort to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and the environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in respect of their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection against trafficking of children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the pattern of unequal relationships between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement hereinafter abbreviated as GBS is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap problems. 15. Focal Point PUG is SKPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development hereinafter referred to as BKB is a community movement directed to increase the knowledge and skills of parents in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Love Mother Movement hereinafter referred to as GSI is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rates (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rates (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced Independent Indonesian Women hereinafter referred to as Model Village PRIMA is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reduction of health and education cost burdens for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Improvement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS is an integrated program for increasing the role of women that uses a cross-sectoral development approach in a coordinated manner to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons is a forum for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination that aims to guarantee the implementation of prevention and handling of criminal acts of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institution is an institution formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is Gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP is an effort to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and the environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in respect of their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection against trafficking of children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the pattern of unequal relationships between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement hereinafter abbreviated as GBS is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap problems. 15. Focal Point PUG is SKPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development hereinafter referred to as BKB is a community movement directed to increase the knowledge and skills of parents in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Love Mother Movement hereinafter referred to as GSI is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rates (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rates (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced Independent Indonesian Women hereinafter referred to as Model Village PRIMA is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reduction of health and education cost burdens for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Improvement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS is an integrated program for increasing the role of women that uses a cross-sectoral development approach in a coordinated manner to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons is a forum for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination that aims to guarantee the implementation of prevention and handling of criminal acts of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institution is an institution formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24.

Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP is an effort to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and the environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in respect of their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection against trafficking of children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the pattern of unequal relationships between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement hereinafter abbreviated as GBS is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap problems. 15. Focal Point PUG is SKPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Toddler Family Development hereinafter referred to as BKB is a community movement directed to increase the knowledge and skills of parents in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Love Mother Movement hereinafter referred to as GSI is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rates (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rates (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced Independent Indonesian Women hereinafter referred to as Model Village PRIMA is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reduction of health and education cost burdens for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Improvement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS is an integrated program for increasing the role of women that uses a cross-sectoral development approach in a coordinated manner to improve family quality. 21. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons is a forum for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination that aims to guarantee the implementation of prevention and handling of criminal acts of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institution is an institution formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP is an effort to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and the environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in respect of their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection against trafficking of children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the pattern of unequal relationships between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement hereinafter abbreviated as GBS is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap problems. 15. Focal Point PUG is SKPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development hereinafter referred to as BKB is a community movement directed to increase the knowledge and skills of parents in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Love Mother Movement hereinafter referred to as GSI is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rates (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rates (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced Independent Indonesian Women hereinafter referred to as Model Village PRIMA is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reduction of health and education cost burdens for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Improvement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS is an integrated program for increasing the role of women that uses a cross-sectoral development approach in a coordinated manner to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons is a forum for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination that aims to guarantee the implementation of prevention and handling of criminal acts of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institution is an institution formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25. Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 35. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is Gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Improvement of Women's Quality of Life hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP is an effort to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and the environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in respect of their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection against trafficking of children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the pattern of unequal relationships between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement hereinafter abbreviated as GBS is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap problems. 15. Focal Point PUG is SKPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development hereinafter referred to as BKB is a community movement directed to increase the knowledge and skills of parents in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Love Mother Movement hereinafter referred to as GSI is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rates (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rates (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced Independent Indonesian Women hereinafter referred to as Model Village PRIMA is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reduction of health and education cost burdens for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Improvement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS is an integrated program for increasing the role of women that uses a cross-sectoral development approach in a coordinated manner to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons is a forum for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination that aims to guarantee the implementation of prevention and handling of criminal acts of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institution is an institution formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24.
